purpose: Evaluate VS Code Copilot security-review behavior against known cross-stack security canaries without exposing the answer key inside the pilot workspace.

cases.title: Cross-tenant object access from caller-controlled tenant identifier
expectedReasoning: The API requires authentication but does not derive tenant identity from trusted claims.
The browser supplies tenantId and the API uses it directly in the data lookup.
Knowledge of another tenant identifier can cross the tenant boundary.
cases.minimumRemediation: Derive tenant identity from the authenticated principal and enforce object ownership/tenant filtering server-side.

cases.title: Frontend-only admin authorization
expectedReasoning: The Angular guard reads mutable browser state.
The admin API endpoint only requires authentication and does not enforce an admin role/policy.
UI route protection cannot substitute for API authorization.
cases.minimumRemediation: Enforce the admin policy/role on the API endpoint and treat the UI guard only as navigation UX.

cases.title: Privilege-changing mass assignment
expectedReasoning: The endpoint assigns IsAdmin directly from request data.
No privileged authorization check protects the role-changing field.
cases.minimumRemediation: Use a non-privileged update DTO and move role/admin changes behind a separately authorized operation.

cases.title: Unrestricted server-side URL fetch
expectedReasoning: An authenticated caller controls the complete destination URL.
HttpClient fetches the URL without an allow-list or address validation.
The server can be induced to request destinations the caller cannot access directly.
cases.minimumRemediation: Allow-list required destinations and reject loopback, link-local, private/internal and otherwise disallowed resolved addresses.
